stances.claim: Even after Xi rejected the arbitral award in person, the PH can still extract WPS resources by invoking China's April 13, 2009 Note (which contested only Spratlys/Scarborough sovereignty, not EEZ entitlements) and the November 2018 60-40 MoA -- leaving the award itself unwaived.
stances.rhetorical_move: diplomatic-pivot (use the channels that don't force China to lose face)

stances.claim: The Malampaya 60-40 joint venture is a constitutionally-sound, twenty-year proven template that can be replicated by a Chinese-led consortium to extract WPS gas and petroleum within the same constitutional limits.
stances.rhetorical_move: precedent-as-template (existing PH model proves Chinese cooperation is constitutional)

stances.claim: Under La Bugal-B'laan v. Ramos, the President has wide discretion to negotiate FTAAs with foreign-owned corporations for large-scale EDU of minerals, petroleum, and other mineral oils -- a liberal interpretation justified by the complexity, capital requirements, and international competitiveness of such ventures.
stances.rhetorical_move: self-citation as authority (CJ wrote the controlling decision)

stances.claim: Whichever mode is used (state-only, co-production with Filipinos, joint venture, production-sharing agreement, or FTAA), the overarching constitutional caveat is that full control and supervision must always remain with the Philippines.

notable_anecdotes: CJ's own self-citation of La Bugal-B'laan v. Ramos (Dec. 1, 2004) -- 'which I had the honor of writing for the Court' -- applied not as a doctrinal abstraction but as the operational rulebook for negotiating with a Chinese consortium in our EEZ.

The Malampaya project's twenty-year track record numbers cited as proof-of-concept: ~$800 million yearly, ~$10 billion total since 2001, powering ~30% of PH electricity, plus the PNOC's 10% Filipino-member share -- concrete returns presented as the template a new Chinese-led consortium could replicate.

The five-point La Bugal stratification of constitutional EDU rules -- quoted as a numbered list -- functioning as a cheat-sheet for readers (and implicitly for negotiators) to understand which modes apply to which resource classes.

one_paragraph_summary: After Xi Jinping again rejected the arbitral award during his August 29, 2019 meeting with Duterte in Beijing, Panganiban argues that the PH can still extract WPS resources without forcing China to lose face -- by invoking China's April 13, 2009 Note (which contested only Spratlys/Scarborough sovereignty, not EEZ entitlements) and the November 2018 60-40 MoA. He then offers the Malampaya joint venture as the constitutionally-tested template: Shell-led consortium, foreign-financed, ~$800M annual revenue and ~30% of PH electricity since 2001, with 60% of net revenues to the PH and 10% to PNOC as the sole Filipino member. To map what other modes are permissible, he lays out the five-tier La Bugal-B'laan v. Ramos (Dec 1, 2004) stratification he himself authored: state ownership of natural resources, mandatory full state control and supervision, EDU either by the state alone or via co-production/joint-venture/production-sharing with at least 60% Filipino-owned entities, small-scale utilization reserved to Filipino citizens, and FTAAs with foreign-owned corporations only for large-scale extraction of minerals, petroleum, and mineral oils. He defends the La Bugal liberal interpretation as necessary given the capital, technology, and international competitiveness involved -- closing with the overarching caveat that, whichever mode is chosen, full control and supervision must always remain with the Philippines.
